meta.name: Invergent
meta.description: An original experimental framework for practicing and exploring divergent, convergent, and switching modes of thinking.
meta.notice: This is an experimental heuristic prototype, not a clinical diagnosis or a validated psychometric instrument.

tasks.question: You have one empty shipping container. What could it become?
tasks.hint: List as many distinct uses as you can. One idea per line.

tasks.question: A school has 30 days, $1,000, and one teacher. Which first intervention is most defensible?
tasks.hint: Choose one option. Focus on constraints and impact.

choices.title: Buy tablets for every student
Create a teacher-led digital learning club with shared devices
Build a new computer laboratory
choices.description: Useful long-term, but unlikely to finish within 30 days.

choices.title: Launch a nationwide social media campaign
choices.description: Broad reach, but weak control over local learning outcomes.

tasks.question: Imagine a city park with no electricity. What could it be used for at night?
tasks.hint: Go beyond the obvious. Try different domains.

tasks.question: A team must deliver one prototype tomorrow. Which rule should dominate the decision?
tasks.hint: Choose the strongest general decision rule.

choices.title: Pick the most original idea
choices.description: Originality matters, but may ignore feasibility.

choices.title: Pick the idea with the longest feature list
choices.description: More features do not guarantee value.

choices.title: Pick the smallest testable idea that addresses the core problem
Pick the idea everyone likes most

tasks.question: A broken smartphone is found in a drawer. What could you do with it?
tasks.hint: Think beyond repair, recycling, or selling it.

tasks.question: You have four proposals with equal cost. Which should be selected for the next test?

choices.title: The proposal with the coolest presentation
choices.description: Presentation quality is weak evidence of impact.

choices.title: The proposal supported by measurable results
The proposal from the most senior person
The proposal with the most pages

tasks.question: How could a school desk be redesigned for purposes other than sitting and writing?
tasks.hint: Generate varied functions, not just cosmetic changes.

tasks.question: A project has 20 possible features but capacity for only 5. What is the best next move?
tasks.hint: Choose the most defensible prioritization rule.

choices.title: Let each team pick their favorite five
Implement the five easiest features
choices.description: Ease is not the same as value.

choices.title: Rank features by user value, risk, and effort
Keep all 20 and work faster

tasks.question: What are unusual ways a map could be used?
tasks.hint: Think across education, art, science, games, business, and daily life.

tasks.question: A survey response conflicts with sensor data. What should happen first?
tasks.hint: Choose the most defensible first step.

choices.title: Delete the survey response
Trust the sensor automatically
choices.description: Sensors can also fail or be misconfigured.

choices.title: Check the measurement definitions and data quality
choices.description: Clarifies whether the sources are actually comparable.

choices.title: Average the two values

tasks.question: Give as many ways as possible to make a boring meeting more useful without reducing its purpose.
tasks.hint: Mix process, technology, environment, incentives, and communication.

tasks.question: A solution works in a pilot but fails at scale. Which question should come first?

choices.title: Who is to blame?
choices.description: Does not identify the system constraint.

choices.title: What changed between the pilot context and the scaled context?
choices.description: Targets the difference most likely to explain the failure.

choices.title: Can we make the presentation better?
Can we run the same pilot again?
choices.description: Repeating without diagnosis may reproduce the failure.

tasks.question: First, generate as many solutions as possible for reducing plastic waste in a school. Then select ONE solution and explain why it should be tested first.
tasks.hint: Write many ideas first, then clearly mark your final choice with “FINAL:” on a new line.

tasks.question: Imagine an empty warehouse. Explore several possible uses, then choose one based on a 30-day deadline and limited budget.
tasks.hint: Explore first; converge second. Put your final decision on a new line beginning with “FINAL:”.

exercises.title: One object. Many possibilities.
exercises.hint: Generate as many distinct uses as you can. Try to cross domains rather than producing variations of the same idea.
exercises.prompt: You have one ordinary cardboard box. What could it become?

feedback.low: Try another domain or perspective before you narrow anything down.
feedback.mid: Keep opening the search space. Add ideas from unrelated domains.
feedback.high: Good divergence. You are expanding the search space rather than repeating one idea.

exercises.title: Choose under constraints.
exercises.hint: There is no perfect answer. Pick the option that best fits the stated constraints and explain your reasoning.
exercises.prompt: A school has 30 days, a $1,000 budget, and one teacher. Which intervention should be tested first?

choices.title: Buy tablets for every student
Create a teacher-led digital learning club with shared devices
choices.description: Lower infrastructure burden and immediately testable.

choices.title: Build a new computer laboratory
choices.description: Useful long term, but difficult to complete within 30 days.

choices.title: Launch a large social media campaign
choices.description: Broad reach, but weak connection to the stated learning constraint.

exercises.title: Change the frame.
exercises.hint: Generate possibilities from different perspectives: user, place, technology, nature, social life, or play.
exercises.prompt: How could an empty city park be useful at night without permanent electricity?

feedback.low: Change perspective. What would a teacher, artist, tourist, child, or emergency planner do with the same space?
feedback.mid: Try one idea from a completely different domain.
feedback.high: Strong reframing. Your ideas are moving beyond the obvious use.

exercises.title: Make the next decision smaller.
exercises.hint: Good convergence reduces uncertainty without pretending certainty is perfect.
exercises.prompt: A team has 20 possible product features but capacity to build only 5. What should it do first?

choices.title: Let everyone choose their favorite five
Choose the five easiest features
choices.description: Ease is not the same as value.

choices.title: Rank features by user value, risk, and effort
Keep all 20 and simply work faster

exercises.title: Find unexpected connections.
exercises.hint: Do not stay inside the obvious category. Borrow ideas from another field.
exercises.prompt: What are unusual ways a map could be used?
exercises.placeholder: A map can be more than navigation…

feedback.low: Borrow a concept from another field and apply it to maps.
feedback.mid: You have several directions. Try crossing two unrelated domains.
feedback.high: Excellent connection-making. You are using transfer across domains.

exercises.title: Evidence beats presentation.
exercises.hint: Choose the decision rule that most directly reduces uncertainty.
exercises.prompt: Four proposals cost the same. Which should be selected for the next test?

choices.title: The proposal with the coolest presentation
choices.description: Polish is not evidence of impact.

choices.title: The proposal supported by measurable results
choices.description: Evidence provides a stronger basis for the next decision.

choices.title: The proposal from the most senior person
The proposal with the most pages

exercises.title: Open first. Close second.
exercises.hint: Spend the first part generating possibilities. Then switch gears and choose ONE testable action.
exercises.prompt: A school wants to reduce plastic waste. Generate several possible approaches, then choose one to test for the next 30 days. Put your final choice on a new line beginning with “FINAL:”.

exercises.title: Constrain the creative space.
exercises.hint: Imagine possibilities first. Then use the constraint to force convergence.
exercises.prompt: You have an empty warehouse. Generate several possible uses, then choose one that could realistically be launched within 30 days with a limited budget. End with “FINAL:”.
